extraction.name: CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images
extraction.description: A paper describing the creation of CommonCatalog, a dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed images with synthetic captions generated using BLIP-2, and the training of CommonCanvas open text-to-image diffusion models on this data.
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We began with the YFCC100M dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed images and multimedia files with Flickr IDs linking to the original data. We re-scraped the images from Flickr based on the IDs in the metadata, excluded non-derivative (ND) licenses, split the remaining images into commercial (C) and non-commercial (NC) subsets, and used a pre-trained BLIP-2 model to generate synthetic captions for the images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: CC images rarely had alt-text captions; many captions were unusable, often containing only image titles, URLs, or non-descriptive camera metadata.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: YFCC100M Creative-Commons-licensed images and multimedia files, sourced via Flickr IDs; BLIP-2-generated captions were produced for these images.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels for captioning; at training time images remained in their native resolution. Non-derivative licenses were excluded, and images were partitioned into commercial and non-commercial datasets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: High-resolution CC images were selected; images with non-derivative licenses were removed; images were center-cropped and resized to 512x512 for caption generation; captions were generated with BLIP-2 and paired with the curated images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic captions were created automatically using a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model. The paper also reports human pairwise preference ratings for model evaluation, but not dataset annotation by humans.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors compared BLIP-2 captions with LAION alt-text and reported that BLIP-2 captions were often more descriptive and had higher CLIP Score, but lower caption diversity (fewer unique trigrams).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: BLIP-2 OPT2.5B; BLIP-2 was used to generate synthetic captions.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that the commercial and non-commercial CommonCatalog datasets and the BLIP-2 captions for non-derivative images are released on HuggingFace with associated data cards, and that the models, data, and code are released on GitHub. No versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the dataset as an open-licensed alternative to web-scraped datasets for training text-to-image models, with the goal of avoiding unclear provenance and copyright concerns while improving reproducibility.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited to Creative-Commons images from YFCC100M/Flickr and is about a decade old, so it is less current than LAION-2B. The paper also notes reduced caption diversity in synthetic captions and domain/category weaknesses in faces, general photography, and paintings.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is much smaller than LAION-2B, is limited to older Creative-Commons images, lacks ground-truth captions, and the models underperform in some categories such as faces, general photography, and paintings. The paper also notes reduced diversity in synthetic captions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of open text-to-image latent diffusion models; the paper also releases captions for non-derivative images as an evaluation set.
